sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-Hong Kong SAR DTA (2000, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation 12-02; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 August 2018 on the Luxembourg Business Registers; RCS Circular 2019/01.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of home country / notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing (corporate shareholder)
Certified copy of articles of association (corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (non-Hague states) or Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of funds evidence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature and bank seal; Apostille if bank is located outside Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory ongoing screening of all UBOs and managing directors against EU consolidated sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists (1267/1988 and 1718), and Luxembourg's national freezing regime under the Law of 12 November 2004; PEP status verified by source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs and may require notarized evidence and senior management approval as per CSSF Regulation 12-02.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online portal at lbr.lu / RCS filings via rcs.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be written in Latin alphabet and may use French, German, or Luxembourgish; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet with a certified translation if a foreign trade name is intended; the name must not be misleading under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial undertakings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of a negative name decision, the applicant may file a written objection with the Manager of the RCS in accordance with Article 21 of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and companies; if the objection is refused, a petition may be made to the Tribunal de l'arrondissement de Luxembourg (chambre du conseil) for judicial review; alternatively, the applicant may select a new name and resubmit via the LBR portal; a valid reservation may be renewed once for an additional 90-day period before expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible: a registered domiciliation agent (bureau de domiciliation) is accepted for RCS registration, but the SCSp must maintain a real and effective office in Luxembourg, a local tax representative, and adequate substance (e.g., local bookkeeping, decision-making in Luxembourg). A pure virtual mailbox without any physical operational footprint is not considered compliant with the Luxembourg administrative substance doctrine and may be challenged under abuse-of-law rules and recent ATAD interpretations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 7% (Low-Medium): unannounced inspections by the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes) and the RCS are possible, with an increased probability in the first year if the entity declares no employees, no physical office, or if the registered office is changed repeatedly.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation and non-confusion certificate request (one-shop LBR/RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (Grand-Ducal Regulation on LBR fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) and ancillary compliance documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard SCSp incorporation (€1,500–€2,500)
Market rate, regulatory supervision by CSSF for domiciliation agents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC/AML compilation for corporate shareholders and individual UBOs (PEP and sanctions screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate per principal; time-based professional fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate documents (estimated two sets)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (apostille) and respective embassies/consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedules and consular tariff; application handling fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of documentation into French/German/Luxembourgish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page market rate for certified legal translations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; specifically Articles 1 through 8, 13-1 through 13-22, and 25-27 relating to the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp); also the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2017 on the electronic publication of companies and associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), RCS Luxembourg, 1, boulevard du Prince Henri, L-1724 Luxembourg; e-filing portal: eRegistre (https://eregistre.lbr.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / Partnership Agreement of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), filed by way of the standard registration application form to the RCS and followed by mandatory extraction and publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SCSp has no statutory minimum capital and no minimum paid-up capital requirement; no capital escrow account is required. Contributions may consist of cash, kind, or any agreed assets, and the general partner may structure capital contributions freely in the partnership agreement; the limited partners’ liability is limited to their subscribed contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: FIRST, the subscribers hereby form a Special Limited Partnership (Société en Commandite Spéciale, SCSp) under the partnership agreement and irrevocably accept the cash and in-kind capital contributions subscribed by the partners. SECOND, the registered office (siège social) is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg, and the general partner is authorized to transfer the registered office within Luxembourg by simple written decision. THIRD, [Name] is appointed as manager (gérant) of the general partner, with full authority to register the partnership with the Luxembourg Business Registers, instruct counsel, open bank accounts, execute logistics and payment agreements, and perform all ordinary acts necessary to start the Cash-on-Delivery e-commerce business. FOURTH, each officer is authorized to prepare and file all required notices and publications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online via eRegistre or in person at the RCS counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search in the RCS database and the RESA database. Submit an application for name reservation stating the proposed corporate name, the legal form (SCSp), and the intended activity. Provide proof of identity of the general partner and the authorized filer. The name must not be misleading, identical, or confusingly similar to an existing Luxembourg or EU protected name.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Copy of identity documents of the general partner and authorized filer
Proof of registered-office address if already known
Brief description of the corporate purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the name, submit a new first-choice and back-up name together with a courteous written explanation of the distinguishing element, or request an administrative opinion from the RCS legal office; there is no statutory prejudice to resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner(s) and Limited Partner(s) acting directly; a Luxembourg notary is required only if a contribution consists of immovable property or a real right therein, or if the partners elect to notarize the deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (acte constitutif) with full particulars: name, registered office address in Luxembourg, corporate purpose, duration (if any), contribution amounts and payment terms of each partner, allocation of profits and losses, vote/dividend rights, role and powers of the general partner, transfer restrictions, amendments, dissolution, dispute resolution, and governing law. Have the general partner and each limited partner sign the agreement; the limited partners may sign by private writing unless a notary is requested.
required_dossiers: Draft SCSp partnership agreement
Identification documents and proof of address of each partner
Declaration of cash contribution or valuation statement for in-kind contribution
Criminal record extracts of the general partner and proposed manager
List of true beneficiaries to be inserted in the beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS or the notary identifies defects in the deed, execute an amending rider (avenant) correcting the clauses, or if the defect is fundamental, execute a supplementary deed and refile; notarial refusal is cured by contacting the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce for guidance or by consulting the Notary on the appropriate legal form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Registration Application with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Luxembourg, eRegistre portal or physically at the Trade Register Department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed partnership agreement, the RCS registration form, and the notarized certificate of signature if required. Include details of the general partner, the manager(s), the registered office, and the corporate purpose. The RCS will check the legality, the name availability, and the proper authorization; upon approval the SCSp receives a Luxembourg trade-register number (RCS number).
required_dossiers: Completed RCS registration form (Form C/C1 or equivalent)
Signed partnership agreement (acte constitutif)
Identity documents and signature specimen of each manager
Criminal record extracts for each natural-person manager
Proof of registered office address
Declaration of ownership or lease agreement of the registered office
Statement of subscribed and paid-up capital (zero if none)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de complément), file the requested supporting document or a written explanatory note within the stated deadline through eRegistre; if the query proceeds from a defective deed, execute and file a corrective rider and reference the RCS file number; late response may be remedied by resubmission on the same file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA and Formal Existence of Legal-Publicity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Publication Office for the RESA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS acceptance, the RCS transmits the core particulars for official publication in the RESA. The publication must occur before the partnership may rely on its constitutive formalities against third parties. The SCSp obtains the final extract (extrait) showing the published particulars; registration is effective from the date of filing of the deed, and the publication has regard to enforceability against third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration order or proof of filing
Final text of the partnership agreement
List of managers and their powers
Registered-office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed, contact the LBR publication desk by written application; if the published extract contains an error, file a correction application with a rectification motion signed by the general partner, and the RCS will republish the corrected text without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Common Centre for Social Security (CCSS), Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) operated by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice, and the Luxembourg Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes) for VAT and corporate direct-tax registration if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register all managers/employees with the CCSS for social security; file the beneficial-owner declaration with the RBE (not public); obtain a Luxembourg VAT number with the tax authority (TVA registration) for business activity, including distance retail, and register for direct-tax purposes. If the SCSp carries on an economic activity requiring a commercial business permit under the Law of 2 September 2011, apply to the Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des classes moyennes; for pure mail-order COD activity, no separate professional licence is required, but the business-establishment authorization may be requested voluntarily.
required_dossiers: Tax registration form (Formulaire TVA / RCS registration extract)
Beneficial-owner declaration (RBE form)
Social-security registration declaration
Proof of registered office address
Copy of bank account opening confirmation
Copy of the partnership agreement and RCS extract
Business-license application form only if the ministerial permit is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any ancillary registration is queried, obtain the request in writing and submit the missing declaration or a corrected beneficiary form through the competent e-portal; late VAT or RBE filings may attract administrative penalties, therefore a cure notice with an apology and rectification is required within five working days; if the business permit is refused, appeal to the Minister within one month or request re-examination through an administrative lawyer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des classes moyennes (business establishment authorizations); for industrial/manufacturing operations: Ministry of Economy – Department for Industry (not applicable to pure mail-order COD retail).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) – generally not required for pure ISIC 4791 mail-order retail; an ordinary RCS registration and VAT registration are sufficient unless the company also operates physical premises, storage facilities requiring environmental authorization, or regulated logistics activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency) – Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Class 4 simple-compliance declaration as appropriate for dry-goods warehousing and dispatch facilities below the thresholds of the Grand-Ducal Regulation on environmental impact assessment (Law of 22 May 2008); a full EIA is not triggered solely by e-commerce/COD retail without warehouses above 3,000 m² or installing significant refrigeration/technical equipment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 5 September 2007 on the discharge of industrial effluents and the Law of 19 December 2008 on water; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from storage and loading areas must comply with Directive 2010/75/EU and its Luxembourg transposition (regulated if storage capacity above 50 tonnes or solvent-use thresholds); packaging waste must be declared under the Law of 21 March 2017 on packaging waste; non-hazardous waste transfer is subject to the obligation to keep waste manifests and the use of authorised waste collectors.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the communal supervisory authority based on the Grand-Ducal Regulation on fire resistance and rescue pathways; structural load inspection and wiring certificates are required for any occupied warehouse/open-office space; occupational clearance includes the safety plan required under the Law of 17 June 1994 on labour safety, fire risk assessment, emergency exit diagrams, and the submission of an activity declaration to the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) if employees are recruited.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD – Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified e-portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign and domestic entities register for a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro d'identification TVA) via form 645 filed electronically with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu after completion of RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) filing. A transparent SCSp is not itself a VAT taxpayer unless it holds a fixed establishment in Luxembourg; the general partner (commandité) or designated operator procures the Luxembourg tax ID and, if non-resident, appoints a Luxembourg tax representative for VAT compliance. The 13-digit national identification number (matricule) is auto-issued upon RCS incorporation and serves as the corporate taxpayer reference.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under Article 168bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR), an SCSp may irrevocably elect to become subject to corporate income tax (opaque treatment), thereby losing fiscal transparency; absent this election, default pass-through transparency applies and investors are taxed as if they earned items directly. No US-style check-the-box regime exists; the Article 168bis option plus partnership-level elections under Luxembourg tax consolidation rules provide the functional equivalent. Hybrid mismatch adjustments under ATAD (Articles 168ter–168sexies LIR) override any double-non-taxation resulting from such elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for the small-enterprise exemption under Article 57 LTVL (no VAT registration required); EUR 100,000 EU distance-selling threshold for intra-EU B2C supplies under Article 41 LTVL; no registration threshold applies to a foreign supplier with a Luxembourg fixed establishment, and the SCSp engaged in mail-order sales with local logistics/COD presence typically requires VAT registration regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing via Peppol BIS (structured XML) for all Luxembourg domestic taxable supplies from 1 January 2026, as enacted by the law of 5 July 2024; no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) is currently operational in Luxembourg. Invoices exported to non-EU emerging-market customers must be issued as paper or PDF unless Peppol is contractually agreed; the AEDT retains full audit access to issuance and transmission records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export of goods under Article 46(1) LTVL where physical dispatch or transport of goods by the seller or a third party on its behalf leaves Luxembourg and the customs territory of the EU for a non-EU destination (e.g., COD shipments to the DRC/emerging-market customers); title transfer is irrelevant to zero-rating. Ancillary logistics, freight, handling, insurance and COD collection-agent services directly related to the exported goods are equally zero-rated under Article 46(2) LTVL, provided the goods leave the EU within 90 days of supply and supporting evidence is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD – Single Administrative Document, or electronic IE-507 exit summary from the Luxembourg customs system)
Transport document evidencing exit from EU territory (CMR consignment note, Air Waybill, or Bill of Lading with customs stamp/tracking)
Commercial invoice in the name of the non-EU buyer specifying the shipment terms, Incoterms, and 0% VAT line
Inward remittance certificate or bank wire confirmation from the emerging-market customer matching the invoice amount and FX conversion record
Logistics service provider's signed proof of delivery (POD) and cash-on-delivery settlement report evidencing actual collection and repatriation of proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Articles 63–68 LTVL, the AEDT may retroactively assess 17% VAT on exports lacking valid proof of departure, plus default interest of 0.8% per commenced month and administrative fines up to EUR 20,000 per deficiency. Fraudulent zero-rating documentation triggers criminal penalties under Article 67 LTVL (imprisonment of 1–5 years and/or fines up to EUR 25,000), automatic disallowance of related input VAT credits, and joint liability of the SCSp general partner and logistics agent; customs-evasion sanctions and exclusion from simplified export regimes may also apply where the 90-day export proof or 180-day FX repatriation deadline is missed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the conduct and prudential supervisor; foreign-exchange and capital-movement competences are vested in the Eurosystem framework and the European Single Market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is part of the euro area and applies unrestricted current and capital account convertibility under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63–65). No exchange-control approvals are required for profit remittance, partnership distributions, or liquidation proceeds. The practical constraints are AML/CFT verification, EU financial sanctions, and mandatory balance-of-payments statistical reporting. Convertibility risk in COD source countries is a commercial treasury risk rather than a Luxembourg legal restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirement exists under Luxembourg or EU law. Export receipts may be retained in EUR or any convertible currency indefinitely. All export receivables must be recognised under Luxembourg GAAP, and foreign-exchange gains or losses are recorded at the transaction date or period-end spot rate. No surrender timeline or fixed conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for low-value, high-volume COD collections if the provider is an EU-authorised electronic money institution, such as Airwallex (Luxembourg) S.A. licensed by the CSSF. The SCSp may hold segregated payment accounts and use virtual IBANs, but the EMI will not provide a dedicated capital escrow function. Legal constraints include the general partner's unlimited liability, UBO disclosure for all partners holding 25% or more, concentration risk in emerging-market corridors, and the practical need to maintain a parallel commercial bank relationship for hard-currency settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorised representative and each ultimate beneficial owner must appear physically before the bank or before a CSSF-recognised notary or consular officer unless the bank accepts eIDAS-qualified remote signature and video-identification. For a SCSp with a foreign general partner and no local substance, major banks normally require a face-to-face interview of the general partner or a Luxembourg-resident corporate services provider holding an appropriate power of attorney before account activation. Remote opening is possible only with a complete Luxembourg domiciliation and substance file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual partnership structure: the SCSp is commonly used for private equity fund vehicles, so banks may assume the account has an investment-fund purpose rather than a commercial e-commerce treasury function.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS extract for the SCSp, the partnership agreement, a certificate of non-registration as an alternative investment fund, an operational business plan for mail-order and cash-on-delivery retail, and a statutory declaration from the general partner confirming the absence of public fundraising and non-qualification under the AIFMD.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Emerging-market COD flows exhibit elevated financial-crime signals due to consumer cash collections passing through third-party logistics agents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master services agreements with logistics operators and local payment collectors, reconciliation reports demonstrating the traceable chain from buyer to SCSp treasury, copies of the entity's merchant identification or payment-licence status in each jurisdiction, and a detailed product and invoice register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The account will process high incoming volumes from jurisdictions with weaker anti-money laundering frameworks, followed by rapid outbound disbursements to suppliers and logistics partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening policy, negative news and adverse media checks on all counterparties, transaction-monitoring rationale, local-counsel opinions confirming the legality of COD collections in each target market, and documented customer due diligence on recurring logistics partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO transparency and source-of-wealth review for passive limited partners who are not involved in management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full register of partners filed with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (as applicable), notarised identity documents, suited anti-money laundering declarations, and bank references for the general partner and all natural-person UBOs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from partners must be channelled by bank-to-bank wire using SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV, with the Luxembourg balance-of-payments purpose code for partnership contributions under direct investment. The bank will require the signed capital-call notice, the partnership agreement's contribution article, and a source-of-funds statement. The beneficiary name must exactly match the SCSp's name and RCS number. Euro inflows are unrestricted; emerging-market currency conversions are executed at the applicable spot rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to suppliers and logistics partners are cleared through SWIFT MT103 for single cross-border payments, MT202 COV for interbank credit transfers, and irrevocable Documentary Letters of Credit (MT700/MT707) where pre-shipment financing or large-value deferred settlement is required. For low-value recurring disbursements under the Airwallex rail, client funds are consolidated into a segregated settlement account and routed via local instant-payment networks, subject to agreed transaction caps and per-beneficiary sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign-exchange forward contracts where the local emerging-market currency is deliverable
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible currencies, permitted only for documented commercial treasury exposure
FX swaps for short-term operational liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps for multi-year hard-currency treasury liabilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership income tax return for transparent SCSp (declaration for determination of partners' taxable shares)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due by 31 May of the following calendar year; automatic extension to 30 November via the eCDF electronic filing system for tax professionals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty generally EUR 50 – EUR 10,000 depending on administrative assessment; plus interest on any unpaid amounts at 0.6% per month; habitual non-filing can trigger administrative tax assessment by estimation and seizure measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) — required only for SCSp exceeding mandatory audit thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of the financial year (unless fiscal year differs from calendar year); public disclosure required only where the SCSp meets large-enterprise criteria
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties imposed by the RCS up to EUR 25,000 for persistent failure; judicial mandatory filing possible; administrative strike-off proceedings may be initiated after repeated notifications to the registered office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Beneficial Owner (RBE) declaration — initial and post-change updating
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the relevant triggering event (incorporation, partner change, share transfer, or any change in beneficial ownership); no separate annual deadline exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines of EUR 500 – EUR 1,250 per violation for individuals and up to EUR 25,000 for legal persons; repeat or intentional non-disclosure may lead to additional regulatory sanctions and publication of violations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit is required for an SCSp if it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds in a financial year: balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million; net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million; average full-time workforce exceeding 50 employees. Tax audits may also be commenced at the discretion of the Luxembourg tax administration.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2020 on the commercial register and annual accounts implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for large consolidated groups or voluntarily.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SCSp must file UBO data with the RBE within 1 month of incorporation and within 1 month of any ownership or control change. The law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing; however, an annual internal review of the RBE record is recommended to ensure accuracy after capital movements, transfers, or changes in limited-partner interests.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General and Limited Partners (capital contributions and transfer history)
Register of Partnership Interests (including pledges and usufruct)
Minute Book of Partner Resolutions and Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – 2,500 per annum (Luxembourg registered-office provision and corporate agency services, depending on service scope)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – 18,000 per full statutory audit; not applicable for SCSp below the mandatory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); municipal rates vary by commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp default is fiscally transparent and is not itself within the corporate income tax or net wealth tax scope. Preferential reductions for taxable corporate partners: 80% IP income exemption for qualifying intellectual property (effective CIT about 4.99%), 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend and capital gain income, notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity contributions, investment tax credits, and branch relief. No general statutory tax holiday for e-commerce COD operators.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Formulaire 100 - Declaration des collectivites) via MyGuichet.lu electronic tax portal of the Administration des contributions directes; non-resident entities may submit through the same electronic gateway with a Luxembourg tax representative; no separate Form 100 for SCSp if the partnership is transparent, but an annual information declaration is required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Taxable partners must also make quarterly advance CIT and municipal business tax instalments; the SCSp declaration itself is submitted once per fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally no later than 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; electronic filing by a registered tax adviser extends the filing to 31 March of the second following year; further extensions may be granted by the director of the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identity: exact legal name, RCS Luxembourg registration number, legal form code (SCSp), registered office address and tax ID.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg SCSp's registered address in Luxembourg; non-resident partners are listed separately, not in this box. Do not use a foreign shell address for the Luxembourg office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partners schedule: name, tax residence country, NIF/TIN, profit-sharing percentage, type (individual/corporate/collective investment undertaking).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporate partners, attach a valid tax residence certificate and confirm whether the SCSp has a Luxembourg permanent establishment. A partner with no Luxembourg PE is not taxable on the distribution; only Luxembourg-source or PE-attributable income is reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates, and currency reporting standard.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SCSp fiscal year; non-resident partners aligned to a different year should still report Luxembourg-source allocations according to the SCSp year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue reconciliation: mail-order retail turnover, total COD collections, amounts settled through Airwallex and local logistics remittance providers, cash deposits and related bank/intermediary statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident partner maintains the merchant accounts, disclose them; failure to disclose foreign payment rails is the primary audit red flag. Reconcile every settlement to underlying logistics delivery reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result before allocation: commercial result adjusted to Luxembourg tax result, including transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp result is allocated to partners. Non-resident partners with no Luxembourg PE should receive an informational schedule only; if a PE exists, include the arm's length branch profit, supported by a functional and risk analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax (communal trade tax) base and rate for the SCSp's permanent establishment or Luxembourg office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner carrying on e-commerce through a Luxembourg PE is subject to municipal business tax on PE profits; a non-resident partner without a PE leaves this line nil and may rely on DTA business profits allocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% tax increase on CIT determined for the taxable partners; after formal demand, an ex officio assessment may add 50% penalty; fraudulent omissions can add up to 100% and criminal fines. Failure by the SCSp to produce information makes the general partner/managing partner subject to administrative sanctions and daily delay fines at the discretion of the ACD.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by a tax-transparent SCSp to its partners because the SCSp is not a dividend-paying collective in the CIT sense. The general Luxembourg statutory dividend withholding tax of 15% applies where the payer is an opaque resident capital company; it does not apply to SCSp profit allocations. If the SCSp is not transparent for treaty purposes, no domestic WHT is levied at source in Luxembourg on allocations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the SCSp itself is transparent, the partner, not the SCSp, claims treaty benefits. For any Luxembourg-source dividend/interest/royalty that is subject to Luxembourg WHT (for example underlying Luxembourg portfolio holdings), the beneficial owner must submit to the Luxembourg withholding agent: (i) a tax residence certificate issued by the DTA country, (ii) a Luxembourg beneficial ownership form/declaration, and (iii) supporting entitlement evidence. Source-level relief may be obtained by filing a dispense certificate request with the competent Luxembourg tax office; otherwise a refund claim must be filed within five years. A non-resident partner claiming business profits cannot be taxed in Luxembourg if there is no permanent establishment and must support that position with the TRC and substance evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law does not impose withholding tax on pure arm's length interest or royalty payments. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive suppresses any source tax when the beneficial owner is an associated EU company. Interest stripping rules under ATAD/Luxembourg law may deny deduction of excessive interest (30% EBITDA limitation), and profit-participating loans or hybrid instruments may be recharacterised and subject to dividend WHT where the borrower is not transparent.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers the Luxembourg Master File and Country-by-Country reporting obligation under BEPS Action 13; the Local File is prepared and retained for all material controlled transactions. There is no de minimis threshold for audit; if requested by the Administration des contributions directes, the SCSp must provide the Local File within 15 days. Controlled transactions in the COD e-commerce business—logistics fees, cash collection commissions, Airwallex processing, and trademark royalties—must be documented and benchmarked at arm's length.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply OFC-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). However, domestic substance-over-form, ATAD GAAR, Luxembourg's abuse-of-law case law, and the OECD 'no PE/letterbox' principle require real substance: the SCSp must maintain its registered office, board/managers' meetings, custody of accounts, strategic decisions, and key COD operational functions in Luxembourg. In mail-order retail with COD settlement, the Luxembourg entity should perform or control order-taking, COD collection reconciliation and risk management; the use of local logistics remittance agents should not be structured to create a PE of the foreign partner. Merely holding an SCSp without functions, employees and office facilities is a fatal red flag.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to declare COD e-commerce turnover or artificially underreporting revenue collected through Airwallex/local logistics remittance providers; keeping two sets of books; suppressing delivery and settlement data; filing a false Form 100.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax increase of up to 100% of evaded corporate income tax and municipal business tax, plus late interest; criminal prosecution can result in fines up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment up to three years; judgment may be published.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or managing partners who knowingly sign false returns or pre-judicially strip assets can be personally assessed to the tax shortfall; the veil is pierced for deliberate fraud, allowing seizure of personal assets, travel bans and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Letter-box / Shell Company and GAAR Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp has no Luxembourg substance: no office, no employees, no local management, all COD operations and settlement functions performed abroad; Luxembourg profit allocation used solely to access treaty benefits or avoid foreign tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration may disregard the SCSp, reattribute its income under substance-over-form and impose a 10-100% tax increase; foreign tax authorities may apply CFC rules and deny treaty benefits; the RCS may strike the entity for false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A general partner or manager that knowingly lent the SCSp to a foreign conduit arrangement may be jointly and severally liable for the recomputed tax, because the corporate personality of the SCSp is disregarded; this can extend to civil restitution and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CFT / Payment Compliance Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing cash-on-delivery collections through third-party logistics remittance without KYC/CDD on counterparties; failing to identify the foreign partner's ultimate beneficial owner; using Airwallex/local payout channels for undeclared funds or to conceal the economic beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of turnover for legal persons under Luxembourg AML legislation; freezing of accounts and revocation of electronic money/payment institution permissions; criminal money laundering sanctions with imprisonment up to five years for the directing mind.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and AML compliance officers can be held personally liable for AML penalties, prohibited from managing financial institutions, subject to travel alerts during investigation and, on conviction, imprisoned and ordered to confiscate assets equal to the laundered amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of arm's length agreements and local-file documentation for logistics, cash collection, IT and royalty transactions; charging no or excessive fees to the SCSp; profit margins not supported by functional analysis; failing to produce documents within 15 days on audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to an arm's length taxable profit, with statutory late interest and tax increase of 10-50%; if the adjustment results from gross negligence, the tax increase can reach 100%; double tax and economic double taxation may also arise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly establish unrealistic transfer prices or direct the concealment of related-party contracts can be personally liable for the resulting tax assessments; the court may impose civil restitution and enjoin continued foreign travel until the assessment is secured.
